request.input:
You repair a Boolean network model of the DNA damage response (a published model, Gupta et al. 2023).
A claim read from the literature was turned into a rule change by a fixed template, and an exact solver rejected the
change: the edited network contradicts behaviours the model must keep (the verification cases). Propose another rule
for the node that still expresses the claim but passes those cases.

Rules are written with node names and the operators ! (not), & (and), | (or) and parentheses. A node is 1 when active.
DNA_damage is the only input. These are the nodes you may use: AKT, AMPK_MAPK, ATM_pH2AX, ATR, BAX, BCL2, CHK1, CHK2, Caspase, Cdc25, Cdc2_CycB, DNA_PK, DNA_damage, E2F1, Mdm2, Myc, PTEN, PUMA, RB, Sirt1, TUG1, ULK1_Beclin1, WWP1, Wee1, Wip1, hTERT, mTORC1, mTORC2, miR221, p21, p53, p53_A, p53_INP1, p53_K

CLAIM: CHK2 activates E2F1   (1 paper(s))
EVIDENCE:
- PMC2745661 (review statement citing other work on DNA damage response): "In response to DNA damage, CHK2 phosphorylates E2F1, resulting in its stabilization, transcriptional activation, and induction of p53-dependent or -independent apoptosis [16],[43]."

NODE TO CHANGE: E2F1
CURRENT RULE:   E2F1, (!RB & ((Cdc25 & ATM_pH2AX) | !Sirt1 | !PTEN)) | Myc
TEMPLATE RULE (rejected): E2F1, ((!RB & ((Cdc25 & ATM_pH2AX) | !Sirt1 | !PTEN)) | Myc) | CHK2

WHY IT WAS REJECTED (counterexamples from the solver; "setting" fixes nodes to 0 or 1, a phenotype is read from the
fixed points; the witness is a fixed point of the edited network):
- V02 (Section 3.2, damage: the four stable fates); setting {'DNA_damage': 1}: missing; expected phenotypes ['apoptosis', 'arrest', 'autophagy', 'senescence'] (exact), found ['apoptosis']; witness fixed point {'ATM_pH2AX': 1, 'p53': 1, 'p53_A': 0, 'p53_K': 1, 'p21': 0, 'Wip1': 0, 'RB': 1, 'Myc': 0, 'E2F1': 1, 'Cdc25': 0, 'Sirt1': 1, 'Cdc2_CycB': 0, 'PTEN': 0, 'mTORC1': 1, 'mTORC2': 1, 'ULK1_Beclin1': 0, 'BAX': 1, 'Caspase': 1, 'CHK2': 1}
- V03 (Figure 3, TUG1 E1); setting {'DNA_damage': 1, 'TUG1': 1}: missing; expected phenotypes ['apoptosis', 'arrest', 'autophagy', 'senescence'] (exact), found ['apoptosis']; witness fixed point {'ATM_pH2AX': 1, 'p53': 1, 'p53_A': 0, 'p53_K': 1, 'p21': 0, 'Wip1': 0, 'RB': 1, 'Myc': 0, 'E2F1': 1, 'Cdc25': 0, 'Sirt1': 1, 'Cdc2_CycB': 0, 'PTEN': 0, 'mTORC1': 1, 'mTORC2': 1, 'ULK1_Beclin1': 0, 'BAX': 1, 'Caspase': 1, 'CHK2': 1}
- V07 (Figure 3, TUG1 E1 + miR-221 KO); setting {'DNA_damage': 1, 'TUG1': 1, 'miR221': 0}: missing; expected phenotypes ['apoptosis', 'arrest', 'autophagy', 'senescence'] (exact), found ['apoptosis', 'autophagy']; witness fixed point {'ATM_pH2AX': 1, 'p53': 1, 'p53_A': 0, 'p53_K': 1, 'p21': 0, 'Wip1': 0, 'RB': 1, 'Myc': 0, 'E2F1': 1, 'Cdc25': 0, 'Sirt1': 1, 'Cdc2_CycB': 0, 'PTEN': 1, 'mTORC1': 0, 'mTORC2': 0, 'ULK1_Beclin1': 1, 'BAX': 1, 'Caspase': 1, 'CHK2': 1}
- V09 (Table 1 row 10, PTEN E1 + WWP1 KO (a prediction of the paper)); setting {'DNA_damage': 1, 'PTEN': 1, 'WWP1': 0}: missing; expected phenotypes ['apoptosis', 'arrest', 'autophagy', 'senescence'] (exact), found ['apoptosis', 'autophagy']; witness fixed point {'ATM_pH2AX': 1, 'p53': 1, 'p53_A': 0, 'p53_K': 1, 'p21': 0, 'Wip1': 0, 'RB': 1, 'Myc': 0, 'E2F1': 1, 'Cdc25': 0, 'Sirt1': 1, 'Cdc2_CycB': 0, 'PTEN': 1, 'mTORC1': 0, 'mTORC2': 0, 'ULK1_Beclin1': 1, 'BAX': 1, 'Caspase': 1, 'CHK2': 1}

Requirements, all checked by the solver afterwards:
- CHK2 must be able to switch E2F1 on and never off: it acts on E2F1 only in the direction 'activates'.
- Keep every influence the current rule has: every node in the current rule must still affect the new rule in the same way.
- Use only the nodes listed above. Do not use E2F1 in its own rule.
- You may restrict WHEN the claimed effect applies by combining it with other nodes, if the evidence context (cell
  type, condition) or the counterexample suggests a condition. Say which condition you chose and why. Do not invent a
  mechanism the evidence does not support.
- If no rule can both express the claim and pass the cases, set give_up to true and explain.

Answer as JSON: {"rule": "<expression only, no node name and no comma>", "explanation": "...", "give_up": false}.

text: {"explanation": "Restricted CHK2 effect to RB-inactive context (!RB) by moving CHK2 inside the existing !RB gate. All counterexamples have RB=1, Myc=0 where current rule gives E2F1=0 but template OR-CHK2 forces E2F1=1, collapsing fates to apoptosis. Preserving the model's existing RB restraint blocks this spurious activation. Evidence describes CHK2 phosphorylation/stabilization and transcriptional activation of E2F1 after DNA damage, consistent with acting on RB-free E2F1; no new mechanism invented. CHK2 remains purely activating and can switch E2F1 0->1 when RB=0, Myc=0, Sirt1=1, PTEN=1, Cdc25&ATM=0.", "give_up": false, "rule": "(!RB & ((Cdc25 & ATM_pH2AX) | !Sirt1 | !PTEN | CHK2)) | Myc"}
